story.head: Round two in Washington
paras: The Capitals won the teams’ first meeting this season, 4-3 in overtime in Washington on Oct 24. The Capitals (10-7-0) lost 5-2 to New Jersey on Nov 12, and the Sabres are winless in three (0-2-1). Going in, the Sabres are sixth in the Atlantic (tied for 18th in the NHL) and the Caps fourth in the Metropolitan (tied for 18th).
This season, the Sabres have been outscored 67-55, but only 40-38 at 5-on-5. On special teams, opponents have outscored them 21-11.

The Sabres get their defensemen shooting (5th) and rarely get pinned in their own end (5th), but don't block many shots (30th). On the other side, the Capitals have had some of the best goaltending in the league (4th), but give up a lot of dangerous shots (27th). They also get the league’s best looks (1st), so the Capitals could find some good looks against the Sabres, who give up plenty of them. The Sabres’ knack for getting shots through meets a team that blocks a lot.

Tage Thompson (12 G / 9 A / 21 P in 19 GP) leads the Sabres in scoring, and Jack Quinn (9 G / 10 A / 19 P in 19 GP) isn’t far behind. For the Capitals, Dylan Strome (3 G / 12 A / 15 P in 17 GP) leads the way in scoring, with seven goals in ten games against Buffalo since 2023-24. Alex Tuch (11 G / 2 A / 13 P in 17 GP) has a team-high eleven goals.

Logan Thompson (7-5-0 / .889 SV% in 13 GS) will likely start for Washington. Buffalo has two options in net: Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen (5-4-3 / .867 SV% in 11 GS) and Colten Ellis (3-3-0 / .873 SV% in 7 GS). Luukkonen has started five of their last ten games, including the last one on Nov 11. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net. Thompson has a .846 save percentage in five starts against the Sabres, well under his usual .912. Don’t read much into it: a goalie’s record against one team rarely holds up.
At home, Spencer Carbery likes to send Protas, Dubois and Tuch out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Benson, Krebs and Thompson.
